title: Siegard handoff record
description: What a handoff is made from: the record an agent fills and `bin/handoff.py --render` turns into the message a person reads. The record holds the opening and nothing else — the state, what needs the person, the door recommended and why, the other doors, what stays as it is if none is taken — and points at the full report on disk for the pending items, commit hashes, measurements and command output, which never enter the opening. `bin/handoff.py --prepare` writes the skeleton: the state a script printed, with `state_from` naming it, each door the skill's own report hands with what its entry point's check answered, and the report's path; the agent fills the rest. The prose is the agent's, in the person's language, and is never translated; the few fixed words the rendering adds are this schema's, per language, under `x-labels`. What this schema cannot express — the ceilings, the closed list of framework terms, a reply word used twice, a state that no longer matches its script — `bin/handoff.py` decides, reading the numbers and the list from here: one home for each.

contract_version.description: Which contract this record was written against.

kind.description: `decision`: the handoff hands the person at least one decision or owed act, and the opening is held to the ceilings. `report`: a status answer or a design conversation — nothing waits on the person, nothing stops, and the body has no ceiling.

language.description: The language the person writes in, and the one every prose field of this record is written in. It selects the fixed words under `x-labels`; a language that table does not hold is a change to this schema, never a translation by the script.

state.description: Where things stand, in one line. Where `state_from` is present it is that script's line, verbatim and cut to `x-ceilings.state`, written by `--prepare` and never by the agent; otherwise the person's plain words.

script.description: `goal.py`: the first line of `goal.py --state` over the goal armed through the framework. `progress.py`: the segment it prints for `slug`, else its whole line, else `x-labels`' `quiet` for a project with nothing live.

project.description: The project root the script was run over, absolute.

slug.description: `progress.py` only: the initiative whose segment is the state.

state_from.description: Which script the state is the line of, and the inputs it was read with. Required of kind `decision`: `--render` runs it again and refuses a `state` that differs from what it prints then.

withdraws.description: What this handoff withdraws from what the same invocation said earlier, in one line; absent where it withdraws nothing.

decisions.description: One block per pending decision and per owed act, decisions first. An owed act is a decision whose door is the act and whose `if_none` is the step that refuses to run without it.

report.description: The path of the full report on disk — the pending items, hashes, measurements and command output the opening leaves out. `--render` refuses a path that names no file.

body.description: Kind `report` only: the answer itself, inline, where it is not written to a file, or the short answer above the full one a `report` path names. No ceiling.

replyWord.description: What the person types to take the door: a letter, a number or a short word, unique across the whole handoff, so one reply never names two doors.

ask.description: What the person is asked to decide, or must do before a named step runs.

door.description: What the recommended door does, in plain words.

why.description: Why this door, in one sentence: what on disk says so, or — for a judgment — that it is one and what it weighed.

reverses_if.description: The fact that would change the recommendation, written as the clause that follows the language's `x-labels` `reverses_if` — `a product owner says an empty order is a valid draft`.

settles.description: Where the choice is the person's own: what each door assumes is true and what on disk or in the person's own answer would settle it.

what_it_does.description: What the door does and what it leaves as it is; for an excluded door, the refusal or the rule that excludes it.

others.description: Every other door, in the order a command printed it — never ranked.

if_none.description: What stays as it is if no door is taken; for an owed act, the step that refuses to run.

invocation.description: The line ready to paste — the one place a skill's name or a command appears, rendered apart and left out of the ceilings and the term list.

entry.description: The skill a door invokes, as its slash command — written by `--prepare` and carried unchanged wherever the agent places the door.

answer.description: `door.py --check`'s first line, or `not checked` where no script decides the door's refusals or an input it takes was not named.

refused.description: Each `refused:` fact the check printed, verbatim — the fact an excluded door is named beside.

why.description: For `not checked`: why no check ran.

check.description: What the door's own entry point answered as the tree stood when `--prepare` ran, carried unchanged. A door whose answer is `refuses` is excluded: `--render` refuses it as `recommended`, and a door it accepts is not thereby recommended.

x-ceilings.description: Characters. `state`: the state line. `block`: one decision's block as rendered, its line ready to paste aside. `message`: the whole message that hands a decision, rendered or free text. `opening`: the span at the start of any handoff that carries no term of `x-jargon`, and where a handoff that hands a decision carries a word of `x-decision-words`.

x-jargon.description: The closed list of this framework's words a person never reads in a handoff's opening. A term of `terms` matches as a whole word, case aside. A term of `english_terms` is also a plain English word: it matches backticked anywhere, and as a whole word only in text that is not English — the record's `language`, or, for free text, text whose words of `english_markers` do not outnumber its words of `other_markers`. A phrase of `phrases` matches as written, case and spacing aside, in any language. A pattern matches as written. A hit names the term, the phrase or the pattern's name, never the text around it. The list is this schema's alone: a word added or removed is a change here.

x-decision-words.description: Stems matched at the start of a word, case aside, in English and Portuguese. `recommendation`: a word that names a door over the others. `own`: a word that hands the person their own decision. Either is a decision word; the first one in a handoff is where its decision begins. Every label under `x-labels` that marks a recommendation or the person's own decision carries one of these.

x-hands-a-decision.description: Read from free text, where no record says so: a handoff hands a decision where its final paragraph holds a question mark, where a line outside a code fence opens with a slash and a letter — an invocation handed to paste — or where it carries a decision word anywhere.

en.quiet: No initiative is in progress in this project.

pt-BR.quiet: Nenhuma iniciativa em andamento neste projeto.

x-labels.description: The fixed words `--render` adds, per language: the mark of the recommended door, the words that open the fact reversing it, the mark of a choice that is the person's own, of what stays if none is taken, and of the report's path; and `quiet`, the state `--prepare` writes where `progress.py` prints nothing. Every other word is the record's.

examples.state: checkout · task 2/2 delivered · phase review · last: implement-task task/checkout/refuse-empty — accepted

decisions.ask: Should an empty order be refused at checkout?

recommended.door: Refuse it, with the message the specification already holds
recommended.why: The checkout rule states that an order needs at least one item.
recommended.reverses_if: a product owner says an empty order is a valid draft

others.what_it_does: Accept it, and leave the rule to be changed first

decisions.if_none: The screen stays delivered and nothing ships.
